question: In the Population Census of 2011, the sex ratio in India is _________ females per 1000 males.
solution:
The correct answer is __**943**__ females per 1000 males.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The sex ratio in India as per the 2011 Census is **943 females per 1000 males**.
 
• This was an improvement from the 2001 Census where the sex ratio was 933 females per 1000 males.
 
• The sex ratio is an important social indicator to measure the extent of prevailing equity between males and females in a society at a given point in time.
 
• States like Kerala and Puducherry have the highest sex ratios, whereas Haryana and Punjab have the lowest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Census**

 
 
• A population census is a comprehensive collection and recording of information about the members of a given population.
 
• The Indian Census is the largest single source of a variety of statistical information on different characteristics of the people of India.
 
• The first complete census in India was conducted in 1881, and since then, it is conducted every 10 years.
 
• The census provides data on population size, distribution, and various socio-economic characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Sex Ratio**
 
 
• The sex ratio is the ratio of males to females in a population.
 
• It is expressed as the number of females per 1000 males.
 
• This demographic indicator helps understand the gender balance within a population.
 
• Factors affecting the sex ratio include birth rates, death rates, immigration, and public health policies.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Sex Ratio**
 
 
• A balanced sex ratio is crucial for the stable growth and social development of any society.
 
• An imbalanced sex ratio can lead to social problems such as increased gender-based violence and trafficking.
 
• It helps in understanding gender disparities and formulating appropriate policies for gender equality.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census Key Findings**
 
 
• The total population of India was recorded at 1.21 billion.
 
• The literacy rate was 74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%.
 
• States like Uttar Pradesh have the highest population, whereas Sikkim has the lowest.
 
• The population density of India was 382 persons per square kilometer.
